etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English baken, from Old English bacan (“to bake”), from Proto-West Germanic *bakan, from Proto-Germanic *bakaną (“to bake”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₃g- (“to roast, bake”).

Cognate with West Frisian bakke (“to bake”), Dutch bakken (“to bake”), Low German backen (“to bake”), German backen (“to bake”), Norwegian Bokmål bake (“to bake”), Danish bage (“to bake”), Swedish baka (“to bake”), Ancient Greek φώγω (phṓgō, “roast”, verb).

definitions.definition: (transitive or intransitive or ditransitive, with person as subject) To cook (something) in an oven (for someone).
(intransitive, with baked thing as subject) To be cooked in an oven.
(intransitive) To be warmed to drying and hardening.
(transitive, figuratively) To cause to be hot.

quote.citation: 2008 October, Davy Rothbart, “How I caught up with dad”, in Men's Health, volume 23, number 8, →ISSN, page 112:
quote.text: My dad told me about his days in the Navy: He'd agreed to be a guinea pig in exchange for a shorter enlistment.  […]  They baked him in the sun.

quote.citation: 1610–1611 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tempest”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene ii]:
quote.text: The earth  […]  is baked with frost.

quote.citation: 1596, Edmund Spenser, “Book V, Canto VII”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC, stanza 9:
quote.text: They bake their sides vppon the cold, hard stone.

definitions.definition: (computer graphics, transitive) To fix (lighting, reflections, etc.) as part of the texture of an object to improve rendering performance.
(figurative, with "in" or "into") To incorporate into something greater.

quote.citation: 2014, United States. Congress. Senate. Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Subcommittee on Aviation Operations, Safety, and Security, Airline Industry Consolidation: Hearing, page 36:
quote.text: Disagreements between pilots' unions are baked into the merger cake.

quote.citation: 2016, David B. Woolner, John M. Thompson, Progressivism in America: Past, Present and Future, page 100:
quote.text: Many of the causes of governmental dysfunction are simply baked into the cake of American politics and will never change.

definitions.definition: The act of cooking food by baking.

quote.text: Taking one of her cakes or a tray of biscuits from the oven always gives her satisfaction and a moment of pride; that is, of course, unless there happens to be some little element that doesn't please her with the bake.

definitions.definition: (especially UK, Australia, New Zealand) Any of various baked dishes resembling casserole.

quote.citation: 2009, Dictionary of Food: International Food and Cooking Terms from A to Z, →ISBN:
quote.text: A fish bake made with cod chunks, sliced parboiled potatoes,  […]

quote.citation: 2009, Rosalind Peters, Kate Pankhurst, Clive Boursnell, Midnight Feast Magic: Sleepover Fun and Food:
quote.text: If you happen to have small, heat-proof glass or ceramic pots in your kitchen (known as ramekins) then you can make this very easy pasta bake in fun-size, individual portions.

definitions.definition: Any food item that is baked, such as a pastry.

quote.citation: 2016, Annie Rigg, Great British Bake Off: Children's Party Cakes & Bakes:
quote.text: Baking parchment should not be confused with greaseproof paper — the former has a non-stick coating and will ensure that your bakes lift out of the tin or off the baking sheets easily, the latter will have the opposite effect!

quote.citation: 2024 May 24, The Press and Journal, Inverness, page 28, column 2:
quote.text: Traditionally made with flour, salt, yeast and a large amount of fat or lard, it is claimed that the beloved bake has fallen out of favour with younger people.

definitions.definition: (US) A social event at which food (such as seafood) is baked, or at which baked food is served.

quote.citation: 1904, Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology:
quote.text: The central episode is the temporary burial of the novitiate; a shallow pit is excavated, and in this a fire is made, as for a fish bake;  […]

I am about to launch a scheme for our local to invest a few dollars in a spot where the boys will know where to find company and pass a few hours or a week-end out in the fresh air and partake of shrimp bakes or fish fries and so forget the on-creeping years.

quote.citation: 2006, Jeffery P. Sandman, Peter R. Sandman, Soaring and Gliding: The Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore Area:
quote.text: […]  also featured a fish bake, a dance, and a beach party[.]

definitions.definition: (Barbados, sometimes US and UK) A small, flat (or ball-shaped) cake of dough eaten in Barbados and sometimes elsewhere, similar in appearance and ingredients to a pancake but fried (or in some places sometimes roasted).
